correctness.rationale: Reconstructed full inverse-of-vertex-and-edge-simplex definition. Each fiber is singleton or cross-shore edge. If image meets both target shores, each fiber singleton and the inverse section respects or swaps shores, hence regular. For independent image, a section exists iff every forced singleton representative can lie in one source shore; cross-edge fibers offer either. Assigning c paired image fibers and remaining singles gives binomial(k,c)(m)_c(n)_c(m+n-2c)_{k-c}, while a>=1 singleton X and b>=1 singleton Y gives multinomial(k;a,b,k-a-b)(m)_{k-b}(n)_{k-a}. Mixed-image injections and idempotents yield displayed H,Q,E. Independent brute-force full-map enumeration matches (all/nonregular/idempotents): (2,2)=(169,16,36), (2,3)=(874,174,86), (3,3)=(4489,756,220); finite checks support but do not substitute for symbolic fiber bijection.
